result:
Perfect! I've set up automatic sync on reboot. Here's what I did:

**Solution: Windows Startup Folder Auto-Launch**

1. **Created `/scripts/start-sync.ps1`** — A wrapper that runs your sync.sh script in the background

2. **Created `/scripts/register-startup-task.ps1`** — Alternative method using Task Scheduler (requires admin; you can run this later if needed)

3. **Created startup launcher in Windows Startup folder** — Added `sentinel-sync-startup.vbs` to your Windows Startup folder (`/home/author\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\`)

This VBS launcher runs automatically every time you log in to Windows, starting your sync process silently in the background. It also logs when the sync starts to `data/startup.log`.

**What happens on next reboot:**
- User logs in → VBS launches → PowerShell runs start-sync.ps1 → sync.sh executes → upstream feed syncs

**To verify it's working:**
- Check `data/startup.log` for the startup timestamp
- Check `data/feed.log` for sync activity

**To remove it later:**
- Delete `sentinel-sync-startup.vbs` from the Startup folder

The sync will now auto-restart after every reboot.
